  "report_markdown": "# Strategy Manager Report

## Overview
Costco operates membership warehouses and e-commerce sites based on the concept of offering low prices on a limited selection of nationally-branded and private-label products [10-K line 00134]. The company emphasizes high sales volumes and rapid inventory turnover, achieved through volume purchasing, efficient distribution, and reduced handling in no-frills, self-service warehouse facilities [10-K line 00134].

The business model is built on a membership format where annual fees are collected, with the majority of members being paid members who can utilize their memberships at all warehouses and e-commerce sites [10-K line 00157]. Executive members pay an additional fee and earn rewards redeemable at Costco warehouses [10-K line 00166].

The company's warehouses operate with shorter hours than many other retailers, leading to lower labor costs relative to sales volume due to operational efficiencies [10-K line 00140]. Merchandise is stored on racks above the sales floor and displayed in large quantities, reducing labor requirements [10-K line 00140].

Costco's core merchandise categories include foods and sundries, non-foods, fresh foods, warehouse ancillary (gasoline, pharmacy, food court), and other businesses such as e-commerce, business centers, travel, and others [10-K line 00143].

## Market Positioning and Growth Outlook
Costco competes globally with a wide range of wholesalers and retailers including supermarkets, supercenters, online retailers, gasoline stations, hard discounters, department and specialty stores, and warehouse clubs such as Sam’s Club and BJ’s Wholesale Club [10-K line 00190].

The company has significant competitive advantages rooted in its low-price strategy, efficient operations, strong brand recognition, and private-label offerings like Kirkland Signature [10-K line 00192]. The membership format reinforces member loyalty and provides a steady revenue stream through annual fees [10-K line 00157].

Costco's membership renewal rates are high: 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada, and 89.8% worldwide at the end of 2026 [10-K line 00167]. This reflects strong customer retention and satisfaction.

Key growth drivers include increases in comparable sales, driven by higher shopping frequency and average ticket size [10-K line 00451]. Comparable sales were positively impacted by a 5% increase in average ticket and 3% in shopping frequency during 2026 [10-K line 00451].

New warehouse openings contribute to growth, with 28 new warehouses opened in 2026, including relocations [10-K line 00415]. Sales from new warehouses were a significant contributor to overall net sales growth [10-K line 00451].

Digital sales also play an important role in growth, with digitally-enabled comparable sales increasing 21% in 2026 [10-K line 00452].

Membership fee revenue increases from new sign-ups, fee hikes, and upgrades to Executive memberships have been a key driver [10-K line 00458].

Catalysts for future performance include continued expansion of the membership base, which contributed to membership fee revenue growth [10-K line 00458].

The company's e-commerce operations continue to grow, offering convenience and broader selections that complement warehouse operations [10-K line 00153].

The company’s ability to manage costs effectively, including through employee compensation strategies and leveraging economies of scale, remains a key catalyst [10-K line 00407].

## Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations
Costco demonstrates strong value and growth characteristics, underpinned by a robust business model and solid financial performance. The company's membership-driven strategy, low-price positioning, and efficient operations have enabled consistent revenue growth of 10.1% in 2026, alongside an 11% increase in membership fee revenue. Key financial metrics support this strength: a return on average equity of 28.4%, strong free cash flow generation of $9.4 billion, and a manageable debt-to-equity ratio of 0.17. Despite minor margin compression, Costco’s ability to scale through new warehouse openings and digital sales growth indicates continued operational excellence. Its high membership renewal rates (92.3% in U.S. and Canada) further reflect customer loyalty and business sustainability.

## Investment Recommendation
**Buy**

### Deciding Number
The **return on average equity (ROAE) of 28.4%** is the most significant driver behind this recommendation, highlighting exceptional profitability relative to shareholder equity and reinforcing Costco's strong financial strength and business quality."
